content.title: About
content.content: Nonfat Swiss cheese is a low‑fat version of the classic Swiss cheese that retains its characteristic holes and nutty flavor while containing virtually no fat. It is made from skimmed cow’s milk, offering the same protein and calcium content with far fewer calories.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Swiss cheese is famous for its “eyes,” which form from gas bubbles produced by bacteria during aging.
The nonfat version was developed to meet growing consumer demand for reduced‑fat dairy products.
Traditional Swiss cheese ages 3–6 months; the nonfat variety often has a shorter aging period to keep a softer texture.
It can be used in fondue, but the low‑fat version requires a longer melt time to avoid breaking apart.
In the United States, nonfat Swiss cheese is classified as a low‑fat cheese with less than 0.5 % fat.

items.title: Rich in calcium
items.content: Swiss cheese provides a high amount of calcium, supporting bone and dental health.

items.title: Good source of protein
items.content: Despite being fat‑free, it still delivers almost the same amount of high‑quality protein as regular Swiss cheese.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: The negligible fat content makes it suitable for calorie‑restricted diets.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: It supplies vitamin B12 and riboflavin, which are important for energy metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Probiotic potential
items.content: Fermentation creates beneficial bacteria that may support gut microbiota.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: Although some lactose is removed during processing, the cheese still contains lactose and may cause symptoms in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Like most cheeses, nonfat Swiss can be relatively salty, which may be a concern for people with hypertension.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: Those allergic to casein or whey proteins should avoid this cheese.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Use nonfat Swiss cheese in sandwiches, salads, casseroles, or as a topping for omelets. It can be sliced thin, grated, or melted into sauces.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the cheese in its original packaging or an airtight container in the refrigerator at 1‑4 °C. It stays fresh for 2‑3 weeks. Discard if mold appears or if it develops an off‑odor.
